THE BOURNE SUPREMACY (2004)
DETAILED SCREENPLAY-STYLE RETELLING
ORIGINAL RETELLING — NOT THE ORIGINAL SCREENPLAY

NOTE: This is an original, scene-oriented retelling of the film's story. It does not reproduce the copyrighted screenplay or dialogue.

========================================
ACT I — A LIFE ALMOST REBUILT
========================================

FADE IN:

EXT. GOA, INDIA — DAY

A quiet coastal town.

BOURNE lives here with MARIE, far from his old life.

He trains himself constantly, unwilling to let his instincts fade.

He still does not fully trust the peace he has found.

INT. RENTED HOUSE — DAY

Bourne and Marie share an ordinary morning.

There is warmth between them, but also watchfulness.

Bourne checks the exits out of habit.

Marie notices, but says nothing.

EXT. TOWN — DAY

Far away, an intelligence operation is compromised.

Money is stolen. Two agents are killed.

Evidence at the scene points toward Bourne.

He had nothing to do with it.

But someone wants it to look as though he did.

EXT. GOA — LATER

A trained operative locates Bourne's location.

He watches the house.

Bourne senses that something is wrong before he can explain why.

He and Marie try to leave.

EXT. ROAD — DAY

The operative intercepts them.

A violent pursuit follows.

Bourne survives.

Marie does not.

INT. CAR — NIGHT

Bourne is alone now.

Something in him closes.

The peace he built is gone.

He understands that his past has reached him again, and this time it has taken something irreplaceable.

CUT TO BLACK.

========================================
ACT II — THE HUNT BEGINS
========================================

INT. INTELLIGENCE OFFICE — DAY

Officials review the compromised operation.

Bourne's file resurfaces.

A senior officer becomes convinced that Bourne is responsible.

Another officer is less certain.

The disagreement becomes personal and dangerous for everyone involved.

EXT. NAPLES — DAY

Bourne travels under a new alias.

He is no longer trying to disappear quietly.

He wants to understand who is trying to frame him.

He wants to understand why.

INT. SAFE HOUSE — DAY

Bourne investigates his own past operations.

Fragments return to him.

He remembers a mission in Berlin.

He remembers a married couple who were not supposed to be present.

He remembers that something went wrong, and that he has never fully accounted for it.

The guilt is different from the danger.

The danger he can fight. The guilt he cannot.

EXT. BERLIN — DAY

Bourne moves through the city, retracing an old assignment.

Agents from his former organization close in.

Bourne evades them with precision that unsettles even himself.

Each escape reminds him how completely his training defines his instincts.

INT. HOTEL ROOM — NIGHT

Bourne studies old documents and photographs.

He begins to see the outline of the frame being built against him.

Someone within his former organization is protecting themselves by making Bourne the scapegoat.

Bourne decides not to run from the organization this time.

He decides to go directly at the people responsible.

EXT. MOSCOW — DAY

Bourne arrives in the city connected to his buried memory.

He locates the daughter of the couple killed in the earlier operation.

He does not hide from her or from what happened.

He tells her, without excuses, what he did.

It does not undo anything.

But it is the first time he has faced the consequences of his old life directly rather than simply surviving them.

========================================
ACT III — WHAT HE OWES
========================================

EXT. MOSCOW STREETS — DAY

A final pursuit unfolds through the city.

The operative sent to eliminate loose ends corners Bourne.

The confrontation is brutal and close.

Bourne wins, but takes no satisfaction from it.

INT. INTELLIGENCE OFFICE — DAY

The truth of the frame becomes undeniable to those still willing to see it.

The senior officer who pursued Bourne is confronted with what she authorized.

The organization's internal rot is exposed, at least partially.

EXT. CITY STREET — DAY

Bourne places a call to someone inside the agency.

He does not ask for forgiveness or reinstatement.

He gives them the truth about Berlin, plainly, without protecting himself.

He tells them he is finished being used and finished running.

EXT. STREET — CONTINUOUS

Bourne walks into the crowd and disappears from view.

He is still without a settled home.

But he is no longer only escaping his past.

He has answered for a piece of it.

FADE OUT.

========================================
STRUCTURAL LESSON
========================================

Fragile peace rebuilt after Act I trauma
        ↓
Framed for a crime he did not commit
        ↓
Personal loss reignites the hunt
        ↓
Pursuit by his former organization
        ↓
Buried memory resurfaces
        ↓
Protagonist stops running, starts investigating the frame
        ↓
Direct confrontation with a past victim
        ↓
Final pursuit and confrontation
        ↓
Partial exposure of institutional guilt
        ↓
Protagonist accepts responsibility rather than simply escaping
